\section[cupiditās, cupiditātis]{cupiditās, cupiditātis — a desire, eagerness}

\label{lesson:LA-C112-cupiditas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to miss, then the Latin for a wish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cupiditās, cupiditātis}
\textbf{cupiditās, cupiditātis} — \textquotedblleft{}a desire, eagerness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{cupiditās} is built on \emph{cupidus}, \textquotedblleft{}eager, desirous\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{cupiō}, \textquotedblleft{}to desire\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-itās}, an ending for a quality.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cupiditās}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cupiditās}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cupiditās}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for to miss, then the Latin for a wish, then say \emph{cupiditās} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does cupiditās, cupiditātis mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A desire, eagerness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[spēs, speī]{spēs, speī — hope}

\label{lesson:LA-C112-spes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a wish, then the Latin for a desire.

Greet the whole day in order: \emph{bonum māne}, \emph{salvē}, \emph{bonum vesperum}, \emph{bonam noctem}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: spēs, speī}
\textbf{spēs, speī} — \textquotedblleft{}hope\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{spēs} is inherited, usually traced to Proto-Indo-European \emph{*speh1-}, \textquotedblleft{}to prosper, to turn out well\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1). \emph{prosperus}, \textquotedblleft{}favourable\textquotedblright{}, and English \emph{speed}, which once meant \textquotedblleft{}success\textquotedblright{}, are often given as cousins.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{spēs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{spēs}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{spēs}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for a wish, then the Latin for a desire, then say \emph{spēs} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does spēs, speī mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hope\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dēsīderium, dēsīderiī}
\textbf{dēsīderium, dēsīderiī} — \textquotedblleft{}a longing\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[quārē]{quārē — why?, for what reason?}

\label{lesson:LA-C112-quare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for hope, then the Latin for a longing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: quārē}
\textbf{quārē} — \textquotedblleft{}why?, for what reason?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{quārē} is fused from \emph{quā rē}, \textquotedblleft{}by what thing, for what reason\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short); \emph{rē}, \textquotedblleft{}by the thing\textquotedblright{}, is a form of \emph{rēs}, \textquotedblleft{}thing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
